name: Allon
title: Simeonite ancestor in the genealogy
summary: Allon appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in 1 Chr 4:37, where he is listed as the son of Jedaja and father of Shiphji. No specific actions or events are connected to his person; he is known exclusively through his place in the lineage. The genealogy to which he belongs is part of the extensive genealogies in Chronicles, which aim to document the historical continuity of the tribes and their belonging to the covenant people. The tribe of Simeon stands out because it received its territory within Judah's inheritance and over time was largely absorbed into the larger neighboring tribe. That Allon's lineage was nevertheless recorded and preserved underscores the emphasis placed on each family's place in Israel's community and in God's redemptive history.

versions.summary: Allon is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon. He was the son of Jedaja and the father of Shiphji. He is known only through this genealogy and played a role in the tribal heritage of Simeon.
versions.title: Simeonite Descendant
versions.reason: [minor] The title contains a typo: 'etterkommmer' has three m's. It should be 'etterkommer'.; [minor] The title 'Simeonite descendant' is very generic. A more descriptive title could include his place in the genealogy.; [major] There is no biblical evidence that Allon was a 'leader'. He is only mentioned in a genealogy with no stated function. His role should be changed to something more neutral, such as 'tribal member' or 'ancestor'.; [minor] The last three events (settlement, expansion, victory over the Hamites) concern the tribe of Simeon in general, not specifically Allon. They can remain as context, but the descriptions should clarify that this is the tribe's general history, not Allon's personal actions.; [minor] Allon is mentioned in 1 Chr 4:37 in a genealogy spanning several generations. It is difficult to place him precisely in the 'divided-kingdom'. Some of the names in the list may belong to the period before or during the divided kingdom. 'Divided-kingdom' is a reasonable guess, but the uncertainty should be noted.; [minor] The phrase 'played a role in Simeon's tribal genealogical heritage' is somewhat imprecise – he is merely mentioned in a genealogy. The wording could be tightened.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. There are interesting linguistic and historical details that could shed light on this person, such as the meaning of the name Allon (Hebrew for 'oak') and the context of Simeon's tribal territory.

versions.summary: Allon appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon in First Chronicles (1 Chron 4:37), where he is listed as the son of Jedaja and father of Shiphri. No actions or events are directly linked to his person; he is known exclusively through his place in the lineage. The genealogy to which he belongs is part of the extensive genealogies in Chronicles that serve to document the continuity of the tribes. The tribe of Simeon is unique in that it received its territory within the land of Judah and gradually became largely absorbed into the larger neighboring tribe. That Allon's lineage was nevertheless preserved and recorded testifies to the importance placed on each family's belonging among God's covenant people.
versions.title: Simeonite ancestor in the genealogy
versions.reason: [major] In 1 Chr 4:37 the order is: Shiphri son of Allon, son of Jedaja, son of Shimri. However, one should check whether 'Shiphri' is the correct Norwegian transliteration. In most Norwegian translations it is called 'Sifei' or 'Sjifei'. 'Shiphri' is an acceptable variant, but it should be verified.; [minor] The time period 'divided-kingdom' is uncertain. The genealogy in 1 Chr 4 covers several generations and it is unclear when Allon lived. Many of the people in Simeon's family tree may have lived in different eras. However, 'divided-kingdom' is a reasonable assumption given the context of Chronicles, which was compiled after the exile but describes people from earlier times. An alternative era could have been 'judges' or 'united-kingdom', but it is not possible to determine this with certainty.; [minor] The last three keyEvents (settlement areas, expansion, victory over the Hamites) do not directly concern Allon, but rather the broader context surrounding his tribe. This is acceptable as context, but one might consider limiting it to events more directly linked to Allon.; [minor] The summary is good and informative. A small improvement could be made to avoid saying 'First Book of Chronicles' and instead consistently use the neutral reference form '1 Chr', but this is a marginal detail.

footnotes.text: The name Allon (Hebrew: אַלּוֹן) means 'oak' or 'large tree'. The oak had symbolic significance in ancient Israel and was often associated with strength, endurance, and sacred gathering places (cf. Gen 35:8; Judg 6:11).

The tribe of Simeon received its territory within the inheritance of Judah (Josh 19:1–9) and was gradually assimilated into Judah over time. The genealogy in 1 Chron 4:24–43 constitutes one of the most detailed sources of knowledge about Simeon's descendants after the settlement.

The reference to the Hamites in 1 Chron 4:40–41 may point to peoples who originally lived in the Negev region. Some scholars link this to seminomadic groups that inhabited southern Canaan in pre-Israelite times.

The genealogies in Chronicles (1 Chron 1–9) serve a theological purpose by emphasizing God's faithfulness to His covenant people through the generations. Even lesser-known individuals like Allon have their place in this context, testifying that the entire community of Israel was counted within God's story of salvation.

In rabbinic tradition, the name's connection to 'oak' has been interpreted as an expression of rootedness and belonging to the land. The oak tree as a symbol appears several times in the Tanakh, often in connection with covenant acts and encounters with God (cf. Gen 18:1; Josh 24:26).
